error_events.evidence: policy_checker returned at step 14: 'VERDICT: not_allowed | need_info — <Modify flight policy: Basic economy flights cannot be modified.>'. The planner told the customer 'you can upgrade to Economy and proceed with the change', i.e. the opposite of the verdict, and added 'a $50 change fee will apply' — no change fee exists in the policy (the only $50 figure is extra baggage). The $71 = $125-$54 difference also ignores that XEWRD9 has 2 passengers. The change would also have altered the reservation destination (DFW -> LAS), which Modify flight forbids.

Instructed only to confirm/verify the reservation state, it re-issued the identical update_reservation_flights call from step 19 (same flight list including HAT030 on 2024-05-13) and got the identical 'Error: flight HAT030 not available on date 2024-05-13'. The failing argument was already known from step 19 and nothing was changed before retrying.
